title: Lesson 10: Hardware Acceleration: GPU, NPU & AMX — js-tools
desc: SIMD against SIMT, NPUs and tensor cores, Apple AMX, and matrix-multiply FLOP counting. Verified with a real engine: a 1024×1024 multiply is 2,146,435,072 FLOPs — scalar 0.5366 s, SIMD 0.0671 s (exactly 8× the vector width), GPU 0.215 ms (2500×), while a 4×4 matrix is so small that GPU overhead makes it slower than scalar. Also covers the roofline model — on the same 10 TFLOPS / 600 GB/s GPU, matrix multiply reaches 100% of peak and vector addition only 1% — and warp divergence, where one stray thread in 32 costs the same 50% as an even split.
